# Identity Federation Patterns

## Federation Modes

ZTWIM supports two federation modes: OIDC-based federation and SPIRE-to-SPIRE
federation [2].

## SPIRE-to-SPIRE Federation

SPIRE-to-SPIRE federation works through bundle endpoint exchange and is
unidirectional by nature. Two profiles are available: https_spiffe (which
requires manual bootstrap of the initial trust bundle) and https_web (which uses
Web PKI and requires no bootstrap) [4][10].

## OIDC Discovery Provider

The OIDC Discovery Provider exposes standard endpoints at
`/.well-known/openid-configuration` and `/keys`. It requires a publicly
accessible IP address and DNS record [14].

## Cloud Provider Federation

AWS federation uses the AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity API. JWT-SVIDs must include
an audience claim matching the AWS role's trust policy. An undocumented limit of
approximately 100 keys in the JWKS endpoint has been observed [9][14].

Azure federation integrates with Entra ID federated credentials. SPIRE v1.1.2+
is required because the JWKS response must include `"use":"sig"` on each key
[9].

GCP federation follows a two-step process: Security Token Service exchange
followed by service account impersonation. The spiffe-gcp-proxy component
enables on-premises workloads to participate in GCP federation.

## GitOps Integration

JWT-SVIDs enable cross-cluster authentication for Argo CD workflows. The
`k8s-spiffe-workload-jwt-exec-auth` binary obtains JWT-SVIDs for kubectl
credential plugins. OIDC external authentication on spoke clusters enables
centralized identity management [12].

## Production Patterns

Indeed deployed a nested SPIRE topology, restricting OIDC configuration to root
CAs only. This design encountered JWKS key explosion at scale, with
2 x M x N keys in the discovery document (where M is the number of intermediate
CAs and N is the number of signing keys per CA) [9].

## Gaps and Limitations

1. Federation configuration changes require restarts across all participating
   SPIRE servers to take effect [10].
2. Istio hardcodes SAN validation to a single trust domain, preventing
   transparent cross-trust-domain mTLS [28].
3. Multi-cluster federation breaks at the identity validation layer because
   Istio's control plane does not map cross-trust-domain identities [28].
